_note: Wizard (2024), a full caster (slots from tables.fullCasterSlots). Base class + Evoker are SRD 5.2 (CC-BY); Abjurer / Diviner / Illusionist are mechanics + original descriptions.

classes.name: Wizard
startingEquipment: 2 Daggers, Arcane Focus (Quarterstaff), Robe, Spellbook, Scholar's Pack, 5 GP
classes.flavor: A scholar of the arcane whose spellbook is an arsenal — preparing exactly the right spells for the day and bending raw magic to precise, devastating effect.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description: You cast Wizard spells using Intelligence, drawing them from a Spellbook. Each day after a Long Rest you prepare a number of spells from the book (shown on the table) plus cantrips. Your spell save DC is 8 + Intelligence modifier + proficiency bonus, and your attack bonus is Intelligence modifier + proficiency bonus. You can copy new spells you find into your book for a cost of time and gold.

features.name: Ritual Adept
features.description: You can cast any spell in your Spellbook that has the Ritual tag as a Ritual, even if it isn't prepared.

features.name: Arcane Recovery
features.description: Once per day on a Short Rest, you can recover expended spell slots with a combined level up to half your Wizard level (rounded up), none of them level 6 or higher.

features.name: Scholar
features.description: You gain Expertise (double proficiency) in one skill of your choice from Arcana, History, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, or Religion (you must already be proficient).

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.description: Increase one ability score by 2, or two by 1 (max 20), or take a feat. Repeats at 8th, 12th, and 16th level.

features.name: Memorize Spell
features.description: Whenever you finish a Short Rest, you can swap one prepared spell for another from your Spellbook.

features.name: Spell Mastery
features.description: Choose one level 1 and one level 2 spell in your Spellbook; you can cast them at their lowest level without expending a spell slot. You can swap the choices after a Long Rest.

features.name: Epic Boon
features.description: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat you qualify for. Boon of Spell Recall is a fitting choice.

features.name: Signature Spells
features.description: Choose two level 3 spells in your Spellbook as Signature Spells; they're always prepared and you can cast each once at level 3 without a slot, regaining the ability on a Short or Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Evoker
subclasses.flavor: A master of raw elemental force who shapes blasts around allies and squeezes every point of damage from a spell.

features.name: Evocation Savant
features.description: Evocation spells cost less time and gold to copy into your book, and you always have two Evocation spells prepared without counting against your prepared limit.

features.name: Potent Cantrip
features.description: When a creature succeeds on a save against your cantrip, it still takes half the cantrip's damage (and suffers no other effect).

features.name: Sculpt Spells
features.description: When you cast an Evocation spell that affects other creatures you can see, you can protect a number of them (1 + the spell's level): they automatically succeed on their save and take no damage from the spell.

features.name: Empowered Evocation
features.description: You add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of any Wizard Evocation spell you cast.

features.name: Overchannel
features.description: When you cast a Wizard spell of level 1–5 that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with it. The first use each Long Rest is free; each further use before a Long Rest deals escalating Necrotic damage to you.

subclasses.name: Abjurer
subclasses.flavor: A warding specialist who wraps themselves in a self-renewing shield of magic and unravels hostile spells.

features.name: Abjuration Savant
features.description: Abjuration spells cost less to copy into your book, and you gain an Arcane Ward: when you cast an Abjuration spell, a pool of Temporary-HP-like ward force absorbs damage to you (its size scales with the spell level and your Wizard level, recharging as you cast more abjurations).

features.name: Projected Ward
features.description: When a creature you can see within 30 feet takes damage, you can use your Reaction to have your Arcane Ward absorb that damage instead.

features.name: Spell Breaker
features.description: You always have Counterspell and Dispel Magic prepared, and when you cast either using a higher-level slot its effectiveness improves.

features.name: Spell Resistance
features.description: You have Advantage on saving throws against spells, and Resistance to the damage of spells.

subclasses.name: Diviner
subclasses.flavor: A seer who glimpses the strands of fate and rewrites a roll of the dice before it lands.

features.name: Divination Savant
features.description: Divination spells cost less to copy, and you gain Portent: after a Long Rest, roll two d20s and record them. You can replace any attack roll, saving throw, or ability check (yours or a creature's you can see) with one of these foretold rolls.

features.name: Expert Divination
features.description: When you cast a Divination spell of level 2 or higher, you regain an expended spell slot of a lower level.

features.name: The Third Eye
features.description: As a Bonus Action you gain one benefit until your next rest: Darkvision, an increased understanding of a language, See Invisibility, or greater awareness of your surroundings.

features.name: Greater Portent
features.description: You roll three d20s for your Portent feature instead of two.

subclasses.name: Illusionist
subclasses.flavor: A weaver of deception whose illusions grow so convincing they gain a sliver of reality.

features.name: Illusion Savant
features.description: Illusion spells cost less to copy, and your Minor Illusion improves: you can create both a sound and an image at once, and shape the illusion as a Bonus Action.

features.name: Phantasmal Creatures
features.description: You always have Summon Beast and Summon Fey prepared, and can cast either once without a slot per Long Rest, conjuring an illusory creature.

features.name: Illusory Self
features.description: When a creature hits you with an attack, you can use a Reaction to interpose an illusory duplicate, causing the attack to miss. Recharge on a rest, or by expending a spell slot.

features.name: Illusory Reality
features.description: When you cast an Illusion spell of level 1+, you can make one inanimate, nonmagical part of the illusion real for 1 minute — a bridge you can cross, a wall that blocks, and so on.
